newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee continues to slide, July at 6-week low.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee continues to slide, July at 6-week low.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures fell sharply on Wednesday, as speculative and local selling continued to pressure the market amid a lack of commercial interest, dealers said.
"I don't think there is anyone there to step in front of this market," said Dean Witter analyst Steve Platt. "Roasters panicked and got whatever they could in April and May and are now covered.
"Speculators got committed hoping there would be a (Brazil) freeze," he added. "And there's no one there to take it from them if they want to get out."

Spot July arabicas sunk 10.30 cents per lb on the day, to a six-week low of 207.65 cents, after ranging between 224.00 and 206.00 cents. Second-month September fell 6.65 cents, to 190.10 cents, while the back months fell 3.80 to 6.75.
The July/September spread also continued to pull back, ending at 17.55 cents compared with 21.20 cents on Tuesday.

After falling well short of its 4.00-5.00 cents higher opening call, coffee prices headed lower as speculators followed-through on Tuesday's frantic sell-off. Traders said downward momentum picked up after the July contract breached nearby chart support at 210.00 cents.
July buying interest below 207.00 cents stopped the downslide and the spot month quickly ran up into positive territory before another round of speculative selling knocked prices down.

"People just seemed focused on pressuring this market," said one trader. "There is a lack of incentive to buy the market from the spec point of view. From the trade point of view, it's not important to buy because it is the season of low demand and they have secured the supplies they need in the near-term."
There was little reaction to news that Colombia produced 836,000 60-kg bags of coffee in May, up 12.21 percent over the 745,000 bags produced during the same month in 1996.
However, the National Coffee Growers' Federation said production from October 1996 through May 1997 totalled just 7.29 million bags, down from 9.9 million in October 1995 through May 1997.

The Colombian Federation production calculations seem to point to production for the 1996/97 year seems set to come in at no higher than 9.7 million 60-kg bags. The lowest official estimate the federation has given for the 1996/97 coffee year so far is "about 10 million bags".
After Wednesday's close, the CSCE said certified coffee stocks fell by 828 60-kg bags as of June 10, to 44,830 bags. There were 7,500 bags pending grading, the exchange said.
